newsitem.title: USA: CSCE says 1,500 bags of coffee pending grading.
newsitem.headline: CSCE says 1,500 bags of coffee pending grading.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said Monday 1,500 60-kg bags of coffee were pending grading in its warehouses as of the close of business last Friday.
The CSCE said there were 250 bags pending certification in New York, while the remaining 1,250 bags were awaiting grading in Miami.
A week ago, the CSCE reported U.S. certified coffee stocks fell to 804 bags, the lowest level since the exchange started tracking inventories in 1980.
The CSCE will release its weekly certified stock data after the close of business Monday.
Traders said the 1,500-bag increase -- about six contracts worth of coffee -- would probably have little impact on the market.
"It is not enough to make a difference," one trader said.
Low coffee inventories have buoyed the CSCE futures market, where prices rose last week to their highest levels since late August.

The tight supply situation resulted in part from a late harvest in Central America, where heavy rainfall took its toll on coffee-related infrastructure. A truckers' strike in Colombia last month also delayed deliveries of the 1996/97 crop to key consuming countries.

Although traders were likely to remain focused on the supply crunch in the short-term, the new-crop exports from producing countries should begin to alleviate the tightness by the December contract's expiry on December 18.
December, which goes into its month-long notice period next week, had an open interest of 9,046 lots as of Friday's close, the equivalent of more than two million bags of coffee.
"The coffee pending grading is no big deal," said one analyst. "There is no question we are anticipating more coffee coming up for certification."
